verdict: The languages cluster (a64e48ad, 47c5e480 on g27-lang, base 4cba6159) builds everything the brief lists, and each piece is connected to something that reads it. Item 1 is built: Person.languages is optional, an older save reads as English native (ENGLISH_ONLY, with a comment saying so), it is set on Genres & Background, checked by validate and cleanLanguages, uses real ISO names, and creation's walk tests were extended. Item 2 is built: a 12% ASSUMPTION share comes from its own decider stream (pro.language, keyed by part id). The new state is read by eligibilityProblems, slateReach, directOfferFor, fitOf (and so casting's chance), and by auditionContext, workContext and unitContext through withLanguage, plus a new gated 'language' step of pro.prepare. The Opportunities card has a The Language row. Item 3 (resumeNow) and item 4 (guide entry career.languages) are built. I confirmed each reader at its file and line. The falsifiability twin, save/load and same-seed stability are all tested. All 15 of my mutations were killed. The schema stays 94 in both pins, nothing on the backend lists the person's fields, posted slate parts are kept in the save and win over regenerated ones (addProjects keeps the first copy it sees), and older-save, migration and career-journey tests pass. Defects remain. The change falsified a player-facing explanation: 'Why It Went This Way' says 'your techniques are N% of the way' but now prints a number that includes the language, so mastered techniques show as 93%. An existing test (b20-guide-wiring) now fails because a record went stale, and the report claims all existing tests pass without mentioning it. Several guide, tutorial and comment passages still describe fit and eligibility without the language.

findings.claim: 'Why It Went This Way' under a settled role tells the player 'your techniques are N% of the way to what the part asks at mastery', but N is fit.demands, which now includes the language term. On a language part the line misstates the techniques and never names the language the engine weighed. Part 9 asks for outcomes explained 'using factors the engine actually evaluated'.
findings.evidence: src/ui/career/OpportunitiesPane.tsx:343: `Your fit for it now: you know its genre ${pct(fit.genre)} of the way, and your techniques are ${pct(fit.demands)} of the way to what the part asks at mastery.` fitOf (projobs.ts:624-627) now folds `tongue.weight * tongue.f` into demands. Scratch probe on a Spanish part with techniques {screen:2, scene:1, comedy:1}, all at MASTERED, actor fluent: demands = 0.933, so the line says 'your techniques are 93%' when they are 100%. Same part, non-speaker: 0.667.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the techniques' share apart from the language, or say both: for example 'your techniques are X% … and your Spanish counts as Y% of a native speaker's', using languageDemand. Add a test that draws a settled language part.

The Finding Work entry's Eligibility read and its refusal list (it answers 'Why can't I submit for this role?') leave out the new language refusal.
